checks: Checked 6b3596acb8604c8b §§1–4 (1)–(3). Verified the row formula and equivalence of the determinant condition to positive semidefiniteness with the two-by-two principal minors.

The smooth maximizing branches touch the nonsmooth row objective from below. At two fully positive rows, signed transfers imply common weighted gradients. A tie gives unequal branch gradients, and with unique maxima the two explicit transfers in the tangent hyperplane give strictly positive second variation.
Checked the same-column boundary formula and all equality conditions. Positive equal cross-products would force both remaining entries below one and hence a strict second AM–GM step.
Independently expanded the different-column differences and determinant. The positive semidefinite form proves the cubic for L>0 and has equality exactly at its kernel. L=0 requires only z=1.

If two edge weights are positive the three-vertex graph is connected, so the fixed top eigenvector yields a positive weighted row objective. Compactness excludes a spectral maximum above one and gives the same boundary classification at equality.

With all capacities positive, equality forces z=Z and t=0, since otherwise the three differences are strict. The cyclic diagonal-zero form gives the exact square of the difference of square roots of the forward and backward split products. If exactly one capacity is positive its square must equal one, forcing two unit entries in that row.

overlap.comparison: Identifies the same numerical cubic region as D_2 for the zero-diagonal geometric-mean downward set. The new result puts the capacity vector of every nonnegative stochastic matrix in that region and classifies equality.
Its stochastic inclusion assumes a zero in every row. The present proof admits all matrices, including all-positive row entries, and gives exact boundary equality tests.
Identifies the cubic as the strict ordinary-triangle downward hull. It does not identify the row capacity of arbitrary stochastic matrices with a point in that hull.

readability: For two positive capacities the proof gives the equality tests in the boundary coordinates. It gives a shorter product test when all three capacities are positive.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The cubic and its equality cases hold for all nonnegative three-by-three column-stochastic matrices, including zero row capacities.
